title: Engineered landfills: composite liners, leachate and landfill gas
examples: How is a modern landfill built?
What is a landfill liner made of?
How much landfill space does a city need each year?

stages.label: Reuse
stages.note: Use things again as they are

explain.say: Fresh Kills on Staten Island in New York was once one of the biggest rubbish dumps on Earth. It closed in 2001 and is slowly becoming a park almost three times the size of Central Park. Modern landfills are designed from day one to be sealed safely. But first, where does a landfill fit among the choices?

explain.say: Last! The waste hierarchy puts reduce at the top and disposal at the bottom. Whatever is left goes into an engineered landfill, cut open on the board. Look at the liner: a plastic geomembrane about two millimetres thick on top of at least sixty centimetres of tightly packed clay. Two barriers together are called a composite liner. Why use two, not one?

explain.say: Because each covers the other's weak spots! Clay alone still lets a little through. Use Darcy's law: permeability ten to the minus nine metres per second, a gradient of one point five, over one hectare, leaks about one point three cubic metres a day. A good geomembrane on top cuts that to almost nothing.

explain.say: Rain seeping through rotting waste becomes leachate, a dark, polluted liquid. See the drainage layer: gravel and pipes carry it to a treatment plant before it can build up. The waste also makes landfill gas, about half methane, which is piped off to burn for electricity. Why not just let the gas escape?

draw.text: Methane traps about 28 times more heat than CO₂ over 100 years.

explain.say: Methane is a strong greenhouse gas! How much space is needed? A city of a million people throwing away half a kilogram each per day makes five hundred tonnes. Compacted to zero point eight tonnes per cubic metre, that fills six hundred and twenty five cubic metres a day, over two hundred thousand a year. Fantastic! Challenge: how would recycling half the waste change that?

faq.a: A landfill designed to isolate waste from the environment, with a composite liner, leachate collection, gas extraction, daily cover and a final cap, plus monitoring of groundwater for decades.
asks: How is a modern landfill built?

faq.a: An order of preference for handling waste: reduce, reuse, recycle, recover energy, and only then dispose in a landfill.
A geomembrane, usually HDPE about 1.5 to 2 millimetres thick, laid directly on compacted clay or a clay mat. The two layers together leak far less than either alone.
asks: What is a landfill liner made of?

faq.a: Leachate is the polluted liquid formed when rain and moisture pass through waste. It is collected by a drainage layer and pipes on the liner and treated before release.
Rotting waste makes gas that is roughly half methane and half carbon dioxide. It is collected through wells and burned in engines for electricity, or flared.
asks: Is landfill gas used for energy?

facts: Fresh Kills Landfill in New York closed in 2001 and is being turned into Freshkills Park.
Landfill gas is typically about 45 to 60 percent methane, the rest mostly carbon dioxide.
